limit.description: While the computers API is on: at most this many computers in the page (500 when not given).

cursor.description: While the computers API is on: the next_cursor of the page before; not given, the first page.

size.description: <cores>cpu-<gigabytes>gb, at most the plan's largest and the installation's; absent, the installation's default computer (Helm computers.size), which the computer then records as its size and is refused as that size asked would be.

name.description: What the computer is called in lists.

sleep_after_seconds.description: How long the computer may go unused through the platform (its create, a resume, a stream opened, and every 30 s while one is open) before it is put to sleep; 0 never; absent, 600. A command left running with no stream open is not use: to let a detached job run on, keep a stream open or set a longer sleep_after_seconds.

idle.description: How the computer pauses when it is not used. Absent, it never pauses.

pause_after_seconds.description: How long after the platform last saw it used (its create, a resume, a stream opened, and every 30 s while one is open), with no stream open and its vCPUs quiet that whole time as its host reads them, the computer is paused in place: its memory and processes kept, its running time no longer counted. A stream that opens resumes it in milliseconds. 0 (the default) never; else at least 60. A job left running that keeps its vCPUs busy is never paused; one that wakes for a moment now and then (a loop that sleeps) may be. Above 0 on an installation whose hosts pause no computer in place, the create is refused (409 cave_code_computer_unsupported).

lifetime_seconds.description: How long after its create the computer is deleted, whatever it is doing (as DELETE does: its disk too): from 60 to 2592000 (30 days); absent, never. Its answers say when, as expires_at. Out of bounds is refused (400 cave_code_computer_lifetime_invalid).

network.description: The network the computer has. none: no network device at all; commands, files and ports still reach it through the relay. internet: the installation's egress, what a computer has without it. Absent, the installation's default. Any other value is refused (400 cave_code_computer_network_invalid); a value this installation's hosts cannot give is refused (409 cave_code_computer_unsupported).

wait_for.description: While the computers API is on: the observed states to wait for, comma separated (or the parameter repeated), such as running or suspended,stopped.

timeout.description: With wait_for: how many seconds to wait at most; 30 when not given. A longer ask is taken as 60, never refused; 0 reads once without waiting.

name.description: What the snapshot is called in lists.

size.description: <cores>cpu-<gigabytes>gb, at most the plan's largest and the installation's; absent, the size the snapshot's sandbox had when it was taken (its size), or with none recorded the installation's default.

name.description: What the new sandbox is called in lists.

A stream that opens resumes it in milliseconds. 0 (the default) never; else at least 60. operations.summary: The field catalog of the one filter language every traffic filter is written in (a monitor's preconditions, datasets from traffic, criteria.test, review, trace search): each field's name, type, operators and values, and the bounds on a filter. trace_retention_days.description: Days to keep request history. null keeps it until you delete it.

raw_payload_retention_days.description: Days to keep request and response bodies. null keeps them until you delete them.

artifact_retention_days.description: Days to keep agent artifacts. null keeps them until you delete them.

history_deleted_before.description: First day of request history still kept after a shorter window was lifted; earlier days were deleted. null when nothing was deleted.

Fields, aggregations, presets and data-driven chart suggestions for a dashboard type.
Run a chart spec over a range and return its series, totals, units, warnings and notices.

Top values of a field, or ready filter expressions when no field is given.

Turn CI checks on or off for the project's repository.
CI suites, their mode, whether they can gate, and whether GitHub has approved checks.
Switch a CI suite between advisory and gate.
Criteria with their trust, 7-day pass rate and daily cost.

Add a criterion to the project's library and get it back with its trust: pass `name`, `kind` (question, output_grader, assertion or code) and `scope` (span, trace, task, or row for dataset rows). A question takes `statement` and optionally `pass_def`, `fail_def`, `na_def`, an `answer` shape (pass_fail by default; score, category, pairwise and answer_match need scope row) and its own `judge` ({connection, model_id, temperature}, a judge of list_judges; left out, the project's judges in their order); a fixed check (kind output_grader) takes `grader_type` and `options` (on recorded units only a check the catalog marks `live`); a trajectory rule (kind assertion) takes `options` with its type; code takes `runtime` (python, javascript, typescript), `source` declaring `evaluate(unit)` and optionally `min_score`. criteria_catalog lists every check with what it reads and costs, every rule's fields, the code limits and the ready-made retrieval questions. From an agent connection it lands proposed; a person's rule, fixed check or code is on at once, and a question waits for a person to turn it on and decides nothing until its judge is trusted for it.
One criterion: its statement, definitions, judge and trust.

Edit a criterion as a new version that requalifies: its text, its `params` (a code criterion's {runtime, source, min_score}), or the `judge` a question asks ({connection, model_id, temperature}, or null for the project's own order).
Stop or restore grading a criterion.
Start or resume a blind 20-item spot check.

How one criterion's failure rate moves over time, by day or hour, split with `group_by` (model, provider, key, agent, prompt_version). Compare two windows (`compare_from`, `compare_to`) or two groups (`compare_a`, `compare_b`): the answer gives the difference in percentage points with an interval and `beyond_noise`. Rates are a judge's answers on sampled live traffic and every comparison is observed, never verified: read `judge_trusted` and `calibrated_share` before leaning on one.
How far a criterion's judge is trusted: catch rate, false alarms, consistency, anchors, drift.
Turn a proposed criterion on with the judge budget a person sets for it: it starts grading, with its monitor and any run over recorded traces asked for with it.

A criterion's versions, newest first: who wrote each and when, which fields it changed from the one before (`changed`), and its full definition, so two versions can be compared. Read one version alone with get_criterion and `version`.
Restore an old version of a criterion: its definition is written as the next version, which requalifies like any edit.

Everything a criterion can be made of, with nothing to pass: the kinds and their scopes, the answer shapes of a question, every fixed check (`graders`) with its options schema, what it reads (`inputs`: output, expected, context, question, baseline, tool_calls or metrics), whether it calls a model, what one answer costs (`cost`) and whether it runs on recorded units (`live`, `reads`, `not_live_reason`), every trajectory rule (`assertions`) with its fields, types and enums, the code runtimes with a template, the unit fields code receives and the limits it runs under, what a test may run on, and the ready-made retrieval questions (`templates`: faithful to the context, context is relevant, answers the question, cites its sources), each with its rubric, what the judge must be shown and one worked example.
Propose a criterion, or a new code version of one; it stays proposed until a person turns it on.

Dry-run a criterion of any kind on up to 25 units and keep nothing: pass `criterion` (a criterion to create, or {criterion_id, version}) and `on` ({kind: recent, scope: trace|task, window_hours, workload_id, filter, limit}, {kind: dataset, dataset_id, limit}, or {kind: inline, input, output, expected, baseline, metadata} for one example typed by hand). Each result gives the verdict, a `reason` code when there is none, the `detail` in the answerer's words, a `score`, and `received`: what the criterion was given. Fixed checks, code and score, category, pairwise and answer-match questions are answered by a worker; code with no sandbox is inconclusive, never passed. Needs payload:read and spends at most $0.25 of judging per call.

Change rows by row_key: values are merged by column (null removes one), tags replace the row's tags, split sets its split. A row's revision, when sent, must be the one you read; every change lands or none does.

Add rows to a dataset without resending it: {rows: [{row_key?, values, tags?, split?}]}, up to 500. The rows join the head; a run pinned to a version does not see them until a new version is cut. A dataset made from traffic takes rows only from traffic.
Remove rows from a dataset's head by row_key, each at the revision you read when you send one. Frozen versions keep them.

operations.summary: Start a run of an experiment and get it back queued: pass the experiment's id and, for less than all of it, a `scope`; read it with evals.result until it is completed. For a task the caller ran itself (an external target) send outputs, one per row and trial, and Caveman only judges them. scope.budget_usd caps the spend and is required over one trial and for a run an agent connection or a project key starts.

budget_usd.description: The most the run may spend, at list prices. Required when trials is over 1, and for any run an agent connection or a project key starts.

mode.description: partial: the run holds only some of the cases (a quick look at a sample). A partial run is never a baseline and never compared. Left out, the run is full.

commit.description: The change the run was made for, as the caller reports it (a CI job's commit, ref, base and pull request). Returned on the run's scope; nothing grades or compares on it.

outputs.description: Outputs the caller produced, one per trial of a row, for an experiment with an external target. The run holds the rows they name; Caveman grades them and never reads them as its own execution.

operations.summary: Reads a run: its cells' inputs, outputs, metrics and criterion verdicts. A caller without payload:read gets the same run without inputs, outputs, reasons or error text. While the run is queued or running, since (an earlier read's next_since) returns only the cells changed after it, without their inputs; merge them by id.
Reads human review notes attached to evaluation cells; requires explicit payload:read scope.

Compare a completed run with a baseline run of the same experiment, on identical datasets and criteria. With no baseline_run_id the baseline is the experiment's saved one, else the project's default when that is a run of this experiment; with neither it answers cave_eval_no_baseline. With no policy the experiment's stored gate policy decides (kernel until one is stored; an eval file's gate.policy, an SDK's gate_policy and evals.set_baseline store it), and `policy_source` names which decided: experiment or query. kernel reads the statistics, which pass on about 30 cases and more; strict fails when any criterion got worse on any case. Returns the verdict (`quality`: passed, failed, need_more_data or incomplete) with a one-sentence `summary`, the numbers per criterion and the changed cases; never certifies savings or rollout authority.

What a run would execute before it starts: rows, targets, trials and cells for a scope, and their cost from the experiment's last completed run. usd is null with basis unknown when a target has no priced cell on record. Writes nothing and starts nothing.

budget_usd.description: The most the run may spend, at list prices. Required when trials is over 1, and for any run an agent connection or a project key starts.

mode.description: partial: the run holds only some of the cases (a quick look at a sample). A partial run is never a baseline and never compared. Left out, the run is full.

commit.description: The change the run was made for, as the caller reports it (a CI job's commit, ref, base and pull request). Returned on the run's scope; nothing grades or compares on it.

operations.summary: The prompt version a caller runs: pass `slug` (the prompt's name) and `environment` (production when omitted) or `version`. Answers the texts, variables, model parameters and tools of that version.

Remove a provider connection and its stored credential.
Replace the stored credential of a provider connection.
Each workload's 7-day pass rate, worst criterion, issues, cost per task, live verdict and judge trust.
What a monitor's rules did: each action fired or kept back, on which unit or criterion, its outcome (done, refused, skipped, failed) and the reason.

Replace a monitor's alert conditions: {conditions: [{id, criterion_id (a criterion of the monitor or "*"), metric (failure_rate, pass_rate, mean_score, judged_volume), window_minutes, compare (absolute, change), direction (above, below), threshold, min_sample, renotify_minutes, recovery, notify: {inbox, webhook_ids}}]}. What the monitor grades does not change. From an agent connection a condition notifies the Inbox only; a person adds a webhook. The seven-day regression rule stays on whatever is set here.

Try a draft alert `condition` against the monitor's recorded Judgments over `lookback_days` (1 to 30, default 7): when it would have fired, reminded and recovered, how many steps had too few Judgments to judge, and how it reads now. Sends nothing and writes nothing.

A monitor's latest run over recorded traces: its window, filter, criterion, budget and spend, its state (proposed, running, done, unit_limit, over_budget, over_run_budget, cancelled) and how many units it has listed and graded. `backfill` is null when none was asked for.

Run a monitor of criteria over traces already recorded between `from` and `to`, at most `max_units` of them, optionally narrowed by a `filter` of its own beside the monitor's, to one `criterion_id` of the monitor (units the monitor already graded are then read again for that criterion alone), and held to a `budget_usd` for the whole run. It grades at the monitor's sampling rate and within half its daily judge budget, only while the monitor is on, skips traces already judged, and stops when its budget is spent; read progress with backfill_status and stop it with cancel_backfill. From an agent connection the monitor and its criterion must already be turned on by a person.

A label from an agent connection is recorded as an agent's and never counts as human gold for a criterion's trust; only a person's pass or fail under a criterion does.
How people who labelled the same Review items agree, counted by criterion.

An agent connection's labels are recorded as an agent's and are never human gold.

section.description: Read one part of the body by its outline index. A body over 64 KiB answers with status captured_outline: its parts with sizes and tool names, no text.

offset.description: Byte offset into the section; pass the previous answer's next_offset to read on.
